  designee, to purchase 36-inch Snap-Tite® pipe from Stormwater Experts for a not

  (All Ayes)

9.  Award Cost of Service Study for Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste Enterprise
  Funds
  1. Awarded contract and authorized City Manager to execute an agreement with
  HDR Engineering, Inc. (HDR) to provide a cost of service study for the City of
  Avalon’s Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste Enterprise Funds for an amount not
  to-exceed $68,530; 2. Amended the Solid Waste Fund budget increasing the Solid

11.  On-Call Consulting Services Contract Amendment for International Consulting
  Services, Inc.
  Authorized the City Manager to execute an amendment to the Professional
  Services Agreement with International Consulting Services, Inc. increasing

  Motion to approve made by Mary Schickling, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.

12.  Amendment to US-Offsite Agreement for Civic Center Housing Project to Include
  Traffic and Logistics Study

  Offsite to include a Traffic and Logistics Study in an amount of $7,000 for the Civic
  Center Housing Project.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Michael Ponce. (All Ayes)

13.  Short-Term Rental Application Waitlist Policy Discussion
  City Council heard a presentation regarding policy options for processing short-
  term rental applications after the maximum number of licenses have been issued.
  There was consensus among Council to proceed with the implementation of a
  lottery-based system to allocate available licenses once capacity has been
  reached. City Staff will amend the policy to incentivize property owners to rent
  their home as long-term rentals while awaiting entry into the lottery queue. The
  revised policy will be brought forward to City Council for formal consideration and
  approval at a future meeting.

4.  Change Order #2 for Cultural Resources Consultation Agreement with Montrose
  Environmental Services
  Authorized the City Manager to execute Changer Order #2 for the professional services
  agreement with Montrose Environmental Solutions, Inc., to continue to provide cultural
  resource consulting for the Five Corner Site Improvement Project, for an additional sum
  of $50,000 and a new total contract sum of $216,128.00.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Mary Schickling. (All Ayes)

5.  Options for City Council in Considering Tenant Protection and Rent Control Measures
  City Council directed city staff to return at a future date with a draft ordinance for further
  discussion. The draft will include the following:
  1. Rent increase cap- Landlords may raise annual rent by 5% plus the percentage
  change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), with a maximum increase of 8% per year.
  2. Relocation Assistance-Landlords must provide relocation assistance to tenants
  displaced under “No Fault Termination”. For off-island relocations, landlords must
  provide an additional two months of relocation assistance.
  3. Tenant Protections-The ordinance will also prohibit abusive or harassing behavior by
  landlords toward tenants, consistent with protections outlined in the City of Los
  Angeles Tenant Harassment Ordinance.

6.  Adult-Use/Recreational Cannabis Discussion
  After discussion, City Council decided to not pursue legalization of adult-use/recreational
  cannabis in Avalon.

Authority.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon to repeal and replace
Chapter 1-8 (Reasonable Accommodation) of Title 1 of the Avalon Municipal Code,
implementing housing program 17 as set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element
and adoption of exemption findings under the California Environmental Quality Act.

BACKGROUND: This ordinance was introduced and all further readings were waived during the
October 7, 2025 regular City Council Meeting.

On September 20, 2022, the City Council adopted the 2021-2029/6th Cycle General Plan
Housing Element. The Housing Element is a state-mandated section of the General Plan which
identifies the housing needs, opportunities, and constraints in the of City of Avalon. The Housing
Plan section of the Housing Element further sets forth the City’s goals, policies and programs to
address Avalon’s identified housing needs, including production of 27 new housing units as
allocated by the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Regional Housing
Needs Assessment (RH NA) for the 6th review cycle.

The Housing Plan contains 26 programs adopted to implement the goals and policies of the
Housing Element. Some programs require one-time code amendments, while others have
ongoing review schedules that require monitoring legislative actions and regular updates to the
Avalon Municipal Code (AMC). Over the next several months, the Planning and Building
Department will bring forth a series of code amendments for consideration to implement all of
the housing programs to ensure the City continues to be compliant with State law. The
amendments proposed at this time are intended to address the requirements of Program #17
(Reasonable Accommodation Procedures).

PROGRAM #17  - REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION PROCEDURES: Reasonable
accommodation procedures ensure disabled persons have equal and effective access to
City programs and services, and that reasonable and long-term modifications to City
employment, building, and zoning rules, regulations, practices, and standards may be made
for disabled persons to the extent required under federal and state disability laws, including but
not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. § 12101 et seq.), Federal Fair
Housing Act (42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.) and the California Fair Employment and Housing Act
(Cal. Gov’t Code § 12955 etseq.).

Households that include persons with disabilities are some of the community’s lower-income
 households, as determined by the communitywide median household income survey
prepared with the 6th Cycle Housing Element. Providing reasonable accommodation
procedures in compliance with State law will address the needs of both persons with
disabilities and lower-income households. Program #17 requires that the City review its
adopted reasonable accommodation procedures annually and revise them as appropriate
to ensure consistency with federal and state fair housing requirements.

Chapter 1-8 was last updated in 2014. After reviewing the existing reasonable
accommodation regulations, it was determined by staff that updates are required to clarify
the scope of the program and to streamline the process for application and approval of
requested accommodations. As such, staff recommends the City Council repeal and replace
Chapter 1-8 with completely updated regulations.

Complete ordinance language is included in the as Attachment 1. It is the opinion of staff that
the proposed regulations fully implement Program #17 of the 6th Cycle Housing Element and
provide for more streamlined procedures and access to reasonable accommodation requests
for the community.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The Avalon Municipal
Code will not be amended, and the City will be out of compliance with the mandated
implementation program set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element.

§1-8.01 Purpose and Intent.
It is the policy of the City to make, as provided in this section, reasonable accommodation
in the application of its policies, practices, programs, and procedures, including its zoning
and land-use laws, for disabled persons, to the extent required under federal and state
disability laws, including but not limited to the Americans With Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C.
§ 12101 et seq.), Federal Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. § 3601 et seq.), and the
California Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov’t Code § 12955 et seq.). The
purpose of this chapter is to establish a process for disabled persons to submit and for
the City to act upon a request for reasonable accommodation.

§1-8.02 Definitions
For the purposes of this section, unless otherwise apparent from the context, certain
words or phrases used in this section are defined as follows:
  a) “Auxiliary aids and services” means qualified interpreters, note takers,
  transcription services, written materials, assistive listening systems, qualified
  readers, taped texts, audio recordings, Braille materials, large print materials,
  other similar services and actions, and as otherwise defined by state or federal
  law.

  b) “Person with a disability” means a person who has a physical or mental impairment
  that makes achievement of a major life activity difficult, as defined by state and
  federal disability laws; anyone who is regarded as having such impairment; or
  anyone with a record of such impairment.

  c) “RA Request” means a request for a Reasonable Accommodation submitted by,
  or on behalf of, a person with a disability.

  d) “Reasonable Accommodation” means providing persons with disabilities flexibility
  in the application of city programs; including city land-use, zoning, and building
  regulations; policies; practices; and procedures, or waiving certain requirements
  when it is necessary to provide meaningful access to city programs or to eliminate
  barriers to housing opportunities for persons with disabilities.

  e) “Review Authority” means the city manager or the city manager’s designee. See
  Section 1-8.03 of this chapter.
   Page 5 of 8

§1-8.03 Review Authority
The City Manager or the City Manager’s designee has the authority to review and decide
upon requests for a RA Request. A denial of an RA Request may be appealed by the
requestor to a designated hearing officer. The hearing officer’s decision is final.
§1-8.04 Applicability
  a) Eligibility.

  1. An RA Request may be made by any person with a disability, his or her
  representative, or a developer or provider of housing or other services for
  persons with disabilities, when the application of a city program, including a
  city land-use or building regulation, policy, practice or procedure, acts as a
  barrier to meaningful access to city programs or to fair-housing
  opportunities for persons with disabilities.

  2. Federal and state disability laws afford no protection to persons with or
  without disabilities whose tenancy presents a direct threat to the persons or
  property of others. Determining whether someone’s tenancy poses such a
  direct threat must be made on an individualized basis, however, and may
  not be based on general assumptions or speculation about the nature of a
  disability.

  b) Eligible Request. The subject matter of an RA Request may include a modification
  or exception to the practices, rules, or standards for a city program or for the
  development, siting, and use of housing or housing-related facilities that would
  eliminate regulatory barriers and provide a person with a disability with meaningful
  access to city programs and equal opportunity to housing of the person’s choice.

§1-8.05 Application
  a) Requirements. An RA Request may be initiated with the Review Authority orally or
  in writing. The City will not require a requestor to use a particular form or medium
  to initiate an RA Request. The law requires the Reasonable Accommodation
  process to be iterative and interactive. City staff will assist requestors in completing
  their RA Request as needed to ensure that the process is accessible to persons
  with disabilities. The City encourages requestors to make RA Requests for
  auxiliary aids and services up to 48 hours before the City event needing
  accommodation.

  b) Administration. The City may create any forms, documents, online portals,
  telephone hotlines, or other methods to facilitate the submittal of RA Requests.
   Page 6 of 8

§1-8.06 Review and Processing
  a) Application Review. The Review Authority will approve, approve with conditions,
  or deny an RA Request in accordance with the required findings in Section 1-8.07
  of this chapter.

  b) Decision.

  1. Request for Further Information. The Review Authority may request further
  information from the applicant consistent with state and federal disability
  laws and this section, specifying in detail the further information required.

  2. Decision and Timing. The Review Authority will issue a written decision
  within 30 days of its receipt of a complete RA Request (including any
  additional information requested under subsection b(1) above). The written
  decision must: explain in detail the basis of the decision under the required
  findings in Section 1-8.07 of this chapter, give notice of the applicant’s right
  to appeal the decision, and be sent to the applicant by first-class mail with
  return receipt requested.

  3. Conditions of Approval. The Review Authority may impose any conditions
  on the approval of an RA Request that he or she deems reasonably
  necessary to ensure that the Reasonable Accommodation will comply with
  the Required Findings in Section 1-8.07.

  C)  Compliance with other Regulations. An approved accommodation does not affect
  any person’s obligations to comply with all other applicable regulations not at issue
  in the requested accommodation.

  d) Confidentiality. Any information identified by an applicant as confidential will be
  retained in a manner so as to respect the privacy rights of the applicant and will
  not be made available for public inspection, unless disclosure is otherwise required
  by state or federal law.

  e) No Public Hearing. A public hearing is not required for a reasonable
  accommodation request reviewed and decided upon by the Review Authority.

  f)  No Transfer. An approved accommodation related to property is considered a
  personal RA Request by the applicant, shall not run with the land, and cannot be
  transferred to another person.

§1-8.07 Required Findings
Prior to approval of an RA Request, the following findings must be made consistent with
federal and state disability laws:
   Page 7 of 8

  a) When housing is the subject of an RA Request, the housing will be used by a
  person with disabilities protected under fair housing laws.

  b) As applicable, the requested accommodation is necessary to make housing
  available to a person with disabilities protected under the fair housing laws.

  c) The requested accommodation would not impose an undue financial or
  administrative burden on the city.

  d) The requested accommodation would not require a fundamental alteration in the
  nature of the city’s policies, practices or procedures, including consideration of
  alternatives which may provide an equal level of benefit.

  e) The requested accommodation will not result in a direct and significant threat to
  the health or safety of other persons or substantial physical damage to the property
  of others.

§1-8.08 Appeals
  a) The action of the Review Authority is final unless appealed to within 10 business
  days of the date that the applicant receives the Review Authority’s decision in the
  mail. The notice of appeal must be in writing. The Review Authority will schedule
  the appeal to be heard by a hearing officer within 30 calendar days from the date
  that the Review Authority receives the notice of appeal. The decision of the hearing
  officer is final and shall be mailed by first-class mail to the applicant with return
  receipt requested.

  b) Assistance with Appeal. Upon request, the City will provide assistance to a person
  needing assistance in filing an appeal to ensure that the appeals process is
  accessible to persons with disabilities.

§1-8.09 Modifications Initiated by the Applicant
The applicant may apply for a modification to his or her accommodation. Any proposed
will be treated by the city as a new RA Request and will be subject to the procedures set
forth in Sections 1-8.01 through 1-8.08 of this chapter.

§1-8.09 Modifications or Revocations Initiated by the City
  a) Review Authority and Findings. The Review Authority may make changes or
  revoke the approval of a Reasonable Accommodation applications when
  conditions of approval are violated, it is necessary to resolve a nuisance, or when
  the RA Request contained incorrect, false, or misleading information.

SUBJECT:  Encroachment Permit to Install a Private Trash Enclosure for
  Trash Receptacles within the City of Avalon Public Right-of-
  Way across from 261 E. Whittley.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Find that the criteria specified in AMC Section 4-9.106 is
not met and not approve an encroachment permit at 261 E. Whittley. Applicants are
requesting installation of a new private trash enclosure and storage of four trash
receptacles within the City of Avalon public right-of-way, behind an existing fire hydrant
and on top of a newly poured concrete retaining slab across the street from 261 E.
Whittley.

REPORT SUMMARY: An Encroachment Permit application was submitted on
September 6, 2025, by Scott and Beatrice VanEvery, property owners of 261 E. Whittley
Avenue, requesting approval to install a private trash enclosure on a vacant retaining
concrete pad behind a fire hydrant for the storage of four household trash cans.

The applicants state the platform area has historically been used for refuse storage over
the past 60 years and the previous wooden trash platform, originally constructed by prior
owners and located on City public right-of-way, was removed by the City during recent
hillside stabilization work. The applicants request permission to install a private trash
enclosure and continue to place their private trash containers on the newly poured
stabilization concrete slab located within the public right-of-way. A site sketch provided
by the applicants identifies the desired location of the trash cans behind an existing fire
hydrant, a utility box, bollards, and soon to be installed guardrail.

The proposed project work:
• Installation of a trash enclosure on the newly poured stabilizing concrete slab. The
  enclosure to accommodate four private trash receptacles and prevent the receptacles
  from falling down the hillside.

Pursuant to AMC Section 4-9.105, City Council approval is required for permanent
encroachments that involve above-ground structures or that may substantially interfere
with the use of the public right-of-way.

PerAMC Section 4-9.106, encroachment permits may be granted if the following criteria
are met:
   (a) The encroachment is necessary or desirable;
  (b) The encroachment does not create a substantial adverse impact on persons or
  property; and
  (c) The encroachment does not adversely affect the public health, welfare and
  safety.

City staff recommends the City Council not to authorize the City Manager or hs designee
to negotiate, set for conditions, and execute encroachment permit for the property owner
on 261 E. Whittley, in conformance with Avalon Municipal Code Section 4-9.105 and 4-
9.106.

The proposed encroachment does not meet the findings for approval:
a) Not Necessary or Desirable: The requested use is for private refuse storage on public
  property. Approval would create precedent for private use of City public rights-of-way
  for solid waste storage, which is inconsistent with AMC Section 9-5305(g).
b) Creates Adverse Impacts: The area identified for trash placement is adjacent to a fire
  hydrant and within the planned footprint of a safety guardrail installation project.
  Allowing private encroachment would interfere with these future public improvements
  and City maintenance operations.
c) Public Safety Concerns: Placement of refuse cans in this area could obstruct visibility
  and hinder access to public infrastructure, particularly for Fire Department or Public
  Works maintenance.

Accordingly, the proposal does not meet the criteria for an encroachment permit as
defined in AMC Section 4-9.106.

The applicants expressed willingness to maintain the area and comply with City permit
conditions. However, because the encroachment involves refuse storage rather than
structural improvement or public benefit, staff finds no basis to allow use of this right-of-
way area for private purposes.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None identified.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Right-of-way protection and infrastructure preservation.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: If the City
Council were to approve the encroachment, it would establish a precedent allowing
private residents to claim portions of public right-of-way for trash storage. This could
complicate future right-of-way management, obstruct infrastructure access, conflict with
current City code, and interfere with planned public safety installations.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: If denied, Public Works staff will inform the applicant of the
Council’s action and coordinate proper placement of refuse containers within allowable
locations consistent with City solid waste collection standards.

posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Transient Rental License Application Waitlist Policy

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt a resolution establishing the Transient Rental License
Application Waitlist Policy.

BACKGROUND: On September 2, 2025, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1227-25
repealing and replacing Article 3 of Chapter 1 of Title 3 of the Avalon Municipal Code modifying
the Transient Rental System.

The ordinance established a cap of 410 transient rental units within the City of Avalon. This cap
includes all grand-fathered transient rental units, all units with conditional use permits and all
units with transient rental licenses.

As of the time this report was authored, the City has a total of 390 compliant short-term rental
properties, including:
  • 91 properties permitted by grandfathered use (including 9 banked units currently occupied
  by year-round renters),
  • 267 properties permitted by CUP (including 13 banked units currently occupied by year-
  round renters), and
  • 32 properties permitted by Transient Business License (including 1 banked unit currently
  occupied by year-round renters).

Ordinance No. 1227-25 also authorizes the City Manager to implement a policy to regulate the
manner in which the Planning Commission considers new transient rental licenses once the
established cap of 410 is reached.

On October 7, 2025 the City Council heard a presentation on potential procedures to process
new transient rental applications and a consensus was reached for City Staff to develop and
bring back a policy that utilizes a lottery process.

The procedure sets forth the following requirements:
  1. Annually, or at a time determined appropriate by the City Manager, if sufficient demand
  exists, the City Manager will issue a public notice identifying the potential number of
  available transient rental licenses, the date and time the application period opens, the
  date and time the application period will close and the date and time a lottery will be
   conducted to determine the prioritized order transient rental licenses will be considered
  by the Planning Commission.
  2.  The application period will be open for a minimum of 60 calendar days and may be
  extended at the City Manager’s discretion.
  3.  There is a $25 administrative fee to file the initial application.
  4.  Applications must be complete when submitted to the Planning Department.
  a. Applicants must own the property for which a transient rental license is being
  requested. A property cannot be in escrow or in any other stage of the purchasing
  process to be considered.
  b. Once the application period closes, the position in the lottery is not transferable. If
  a property is sold or otherwise transferred, the application is removed from the
  lottery process.
  5.  At the conclusion of the application period, each valid and complete application will be
  assigned one entry into a random lottery which will be conducted and held during a
  Planning Commission meeting to determine waitlist position on all approved applications.
  6.  After the lottery, the applicants will be notified and prioritized in the order established by
  the lottery. The list will be published on the City’s website as well as at City Hall.
  7.  Once appropriate fees have been paid, applications will have the opportunity to be heard
  by the Planning Commission in the order established by the lottery.
  8.  Once all available TRLs are filled under the cap, all remaining applications will be rejected.

City Staff propose adding an additional lottery entry for property owners that meet any of the
following criteria:
  a. Applicant owns property(s) occupied by a long-term tenant.
  b. Applicant has participated in a previous TRL lottery and been rejected. One
  additional entry will be allotted for each prior TRL lottery entered for the same
  property.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: City Staff will not have
clear direction on how to process and/or prioritize applications for transient rental licenses once
the maximum number of licenses has been issued.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

SUBJECT:  Green Pleasure Pier Renovation  —  Electrical Upgrade

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve the location for the installation of electrical equipment
to support operations of the Green Pleasure Pier.

BACKGROUND: The Green Pleasure Pier is in need of significant structural repairs. In 2018,
City Staff developed a long-term maintenance plan including phased repair and replacement of
the structural piles and decking. In 2024, the City replaced 17 structural piles and 5 fender piles
for a total contract price of $1.3 million budgeted in the FY 24-25 CIP Plan, Project #1 80049.
This project was funded through the Harbor CIP Fund.

The next phase of rehabilitation of the Green Pleasure Pier will include an upgrade to the
electrical infrastructure and replacement of the pier’s deck surface.

The electrical upgrade will require the installation of a large electric service panel (similar to what
was installed at the Fuel Dock). There are three constraints City Staff, engineers and consultants
had to consider when determining the most appropriate location for the panel:

  1. It must be located a minimum of 2 feet above the high-water line. (The existing seawall
  can be used to visually approximate this location.)
  2. It cannot be located too far a distance away from the pier. The further it is from the pier,
  the larger size conduit would be required.
  3. The location must be able to accommodate a footprint that is approximately 8 feet wide,
  2 feet deep and 8-12 feet high with a minimum of 3 feet of level space in front of the panel.

Considering the constraints, City Staff examined several locations. Some potential locations
would require the elimination of commercial lease space, tenant relocation, modification of
landscaping, etc.

Considering the options, Staff selected a location adjacent to a section of exterior wall of a
commercial lease space for Yoshi’s on the north-westerly side of the base of the Green Pleasure
Pier. This location will require remodeling the adjacent wall to remove an existing bay window
used as retail display space for Yoshi’s. However, no other tenants will be adversely affected or
need relocation. The design of the enclosure that will surround the panel will have architectural
features to blend it into the building as well as provide the possibility of a public art installation.
 In FY 25-26 the City allocated $500,000 to support this project. The City is currently seeking
grant funding; however, at this time, this project is scheduled to be funded through the Harbor
CIP Fund.

Though Staff would like the next phase of the Green Pleasure Pier Rehabilitation Project to
include the electrical upgrade as well as replacement of the decking, the electrical upgrade is a
priority to be completed in this Fiscal Year.

In order to continue to develop the project plan set, City Staff request the City Council approve
the site plan for the installation of electrical equipment to support operations of the Green
Pleasure Pier.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: City Staff will not have
clear direction on how to proceed with renovations to the Green Pleasure Pier.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.
